messages.subject: Writing external logs within trajectory
parts:
I would like to be able to write to external logs in a "clean" fashion, however at the moment the only way I have worked out to do this is rather clunky -- I wrap it inside a call to log_
E.g.

########################
myTrajectory <- trajectory() %>%
  do some stuff %>%
  log_(function() {
    fwrite(x = useful stuff, file = "myLog.csv")
    return("Some string I have no interest in seeing on screen")
  }, level = 1000) %>%
  do some more stuff
########################

I am hoping I have missed something simpler / better? I did try adding "level = 1000" to the call to log_, but it still displayed the message on screen. But even if that had worked it would still be preferable not to do this wrapping.

Cheers,
Rob.

messages.author: 0f5b7adb7e70bd8b
messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Writing external logs within trajectory
parts:
On Tue, 22 Oct 2019 at 04:25, Rob Foxall <rfox...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> I would like to be able to write to external logs in a "clean" fashion, however at the moment the only way I have worked out to do this is rather clunky -- I wrap it inside a call to log_
> E.g.
>
> ########################
> myTrajectory <- trajectory() %>%
> do some stuff %>%
> log_(function() {
> fwrite(x = useful stuff, file = "myLog.csv")
> return("Some string I have no interest in seeing on screen")
> }, level = 1000) %>%
> do some more stuff
> ########################
>
> I am hoping I have missed something simpler / better?

Please, do keep in mind that logs are intended just for debugging
purposes. All the system changes are recorded and can be retrieved
with the get_mon_*() family of functions, so you should use these
data, and not the output from logs, to analyse the simulation.

If you still want to collect the logs into an external file, R has
utilities to redirect the standard output wherever you want. For
example, you could just call sink("somefile.txt") prior to the
simulation to redirect everything to "somefile.txt", and then
sink(NULL) to get the output back in your interactive session. See
help(sink) for further details.
> I did try adding "level = 1000" to the call to log_, but it still displayed the message on screen. But even if that had worked it would still be preferable not to do this wrapping.

The log level is intended to mute the output based on the overall log
level, so that you can debug your model or put it into production
without modifying your trajectories. E.g.,

library(simmer)

t <- trajectory() %>%
log_("something", level=1) %>%
log_("repeated message", level=2) %>%
rollback(1, 1)

# all the messages are printed
simmer(log_level=2) %>%
add_generator("dummy", t, at(0)) %>%
run() %>% invisible()
#> 0: dummy0: something
#> 0: dummy0: repeated message
#> 0: dummy0: repeated message

# just "something" is printed
simmer(log_level=1) %>%
add_generator("dummy", t, at(0)) %>%
run() %>% invisible()
#> 0: dummy0: something

# silent
simmer(log_level=0) %>%
add_generator("dummy", t, at(0)) %>%
run() %>% invisible()

Iñaki

messages.author: 0f5b7adb7e70bd8b
messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Writing external logs within trajectory
parts:
On Mon, 28 Oct 2019 at 03:08, Rob Foxall <rfox...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Thank-you for your suggestions, however my simulation models require the writing of multiple bespoke logs. To this end I am currently wrapping my fwrite statement within a timeout that returns 0.

I still don't recommend this method. There are better ways too to
split the logs into multiple files. This is rather straightforward
using awk. Consider the following code:

##################################

library(simmer)

t <- trajectory() %>%

log_("line 1...@filename1.txt") %>%
log_("line 2...@filename2.txt")

simmer() %>%
add_generator("dummy", t, at(0, 1)) %>%
run() %>% invisible
##################################

If this is in the file test.R, then

Rscript test.R | awk -F"@" '{print $1 > $2}'

will run the simulation and send the first log_ to filename1.txt and
the second one to filename2.txt
> My follow-up question is that will an arrival that enters a timeout of zero be guaranteed to "immediately" execute statements following this zero timeout

No, it's not guaranteed.

Iñaki
